name: Forskolin mesotherapy

card.summary: A mesotherapy approach in which forskolin, a plant-derived lipolytic compound, is injected in small amounts into fat to reduce localised fat pockets.
card.note: Not an approved fat-reduction treatment; injected cosmetic mixtures are not standardised.

quick.overview:
Forskolin mesotherapy refers to the use of forskolin, a compound from the Indian coleus plant, among the substances injected in mesotherapy for localised fat. Forskolin raises cyclic AMP inside cells, a signal involved in the breakdown of stored fat, which is why it is proposed as a lipolytic agent for contouring the chin, abdomen or thighs.

Mesotherapy itself uses very small injections into or under the skin. No clinical trials of injected forskolin for cosmetic fat reduction are available; the evidence is laboratory and animal research on forskolin and fat.
quick.how: In clinics that offer mesotherapy, practitioners inject small amounts of a mixture into the target area in repeated sessions. Forskolin-containing products are also sold in oral and topical forms, which are different from injection. Details of mixtures vary by clinic and are not described here.
quick.risks: Mesotherapy in general has been linked to skin infections, including a cluster of abscesses and a mycobacterial infection in one Australian salon, and the FDA-approved injectable for fat reduction is deoxycholic acid for under the chin only. Forskolin injection for cosmetic use is not an approved product.

lead: Forskolin mesotherapy is the use of forskolin, a labdane diterpene from the plant Coleus forskohlii (Indian coleus), as an injected lipolytic agent in mesotherapy, the technique of delivering small amounts of substances into the skin or the fat beneath it [1][2]. People seek it to reduce small, localised fat deposits.

Forskolin activates adenylyl cyclase, raising intracellular cyclic AMP, and is widely used in laboratories for that purpose [3]. Increased cAMP is linked to lipolysis, which underlies the rationale for fat-focused use.

Mesotherapy was pioneered by Michel Pistor, the term was coined by the French press in 1958, and the French Académie Nationale de Médecine recognised it as a specialty in 1987 [2]. Early forskolin weight-loss research was described as low quality and inconclusive, and animal work suggests it can mitigate diet-induced obesity depending on bioavailability [3].

chain: Forskolin raises cAMP in fat cells
angle.text: Proponents inject forskolin into localised fat to promote lipolysis and a slimmer contour. The mechanism is established in lab work, while cosmetic results from injection have not been shown in trials.

infobox: Not approved as a cosmetic fat-reduction injectable

paras: Mesotherapy places small volumes of drugs, enzymes, hormones, plant extracts or vitamins in the skin or subcutaneous fat [2]. Forskolin is one of the plant extracts discussed in this context for fat reduction. It is a lipolytic signalling activator rather than a fat-dissolving detergent.

Forskolin raises cAMP by activating adenylyl cyclase, with downstream effects via protein kinase A and EPAC1 [3]. Derivatives such as colforsin daropate have been studied for conditions like bronchoconstriction and heart failure [3].

A description of mesotherapy states it has no proven clinical efficacy for cosmetic uses and has not been tested in standard clinical trials; the American Society for Dermatologic Surgery said more study is needed [2]. The only FDA-approved injectable for fat reduction is deoxycholic acid (Kybella) for fat below the chin, approved in 2015 [2]. Forskolin research has mostly been laboratory work, including injectable nanomedicine studies in animals [3].

Mesotherapy has been associated with infections: salon clients in Australia developed abscesses and one a mycobacterial infection [2]. France briefly banned the practice in 2011 before the ban was lifted after investigators traced problems to unhygienic conditions, and several South American countries have banned it [2].
No studies found. Forskolin's effects on fat have been explored in laboratory and animal research, and early weight-loss work was low quality and inconclusive [3].

timeline.event: The term mesotherapy is coined by the French press. [2]
French Academy of Medicine recognises mesotherapy as a specialty. [2]
FDA approves deoxycholic acid for submental fat. [2]
